market.what: 1,4-dioxane treatment for drinking water wells and groundwater (UV/ozone AOP, Ambersorb), mainly US
market.method: Long Island 185 wells ~$840M capex over ~6 yr = ~$140M/yr + AOP O&M + rest of US (6.9% of 4,864 UCMR3 systems >0.35 ug/L) + site remediation; est.

value.logic: AOP O&M $1.5-3.5/kgal vs sorbent ~$0.5-1 -> save ~$1.5/kgal on ~27 bn gal/yr (LI) = ~$40M; capex AOP $2.5M vs ~$1M vessel x ~500 US wells, annualized ~$50M; x2 for rest of US/remediation -> ~$150M/yr
value.revenue_logic: ~10% of ~$100M/yr media/O&M pool by yr 7, via a system integrator (ECT2/Montrose style)
value.margin_logic: specialty synthetic media like Ambersorb 560; small volume, high price

trend.drivers: NY MCL 1 ug/L; Long Island buildout; EPA TSCA unreasonable-risk finding (Nov 2024, drinking-water cancer risk); CCL 5; CA NL 1 ug/L; est. CAGR
trend.deadline: NY MCL deferrals running out; TSCA risk-management rule pending (due Nov 2025, delayed)

competition.notes: AOP dominates Long Island (56 AOP systems built/in construction at SCWA). Ambersorb 560 is the only selective sorbent; lower life-cycle cost than AOP. Allonnia >$100M total, $20M+ Dec 2025

lab.synth: macrocycle/polymer/resin: dioxane is neutral and small, needs a porous polymer or grafted bead
lab.test: batch isotherm + RSSCT on groundwater at 1-50 ug/L; 1,4-dioxane by EPA 522 (SPE GC/MS SIM) at Eurofins/Pace
lab.logic: 10-12 wk synth with 3 variants ($30k) + 4 wk tests; ~60 EPA 522 x ~$150-250 (est.) = ~$12k + column work ~$8k

sale.gates: NSF/ANSI 61; NY DOH / county health dept design approval; 6-12 mo pilot vs AOP
